provenance: blind generalization: truth derived from the contract and the sources without consulting tool output or implementation
source_of_truth: Read by hand. OrdersTable.vue calls useAsyncData (no generic argument) and destructures data/status/error, which per the contract makes it a data view. Its template renders four of the five doctrine states — loading (`status === 'pending'` → USkeleton), error (`v-else-if="error"` → UAlert with retry), empty (`v-else-if="!data?.length"`), success (UTable) — and has no partial state (no pagination, load-more, hasMore, stale or refreshing branch). The contract's five states are loading, empty, error, partial, success; so dataView.missing should be exactly [partial] and the finding is heuristic by definition. PriceTag.vue has no useAsyncData/useFetch and no async/pending/status prop (its props are amount and currency), so it is not a data view. Both are documented by a leading comment and exported from the barrel; both have plain element roots, so no wrapper finding applies.

expected.rationale: data view (useAsyncData) with loading, error, empty and success branches but no partial state; the contract's finding fires when missing is non-empty, and only partial is missing here

forbidden.why_not_a_defect: not a data view: no useAsyncData/useFetch and no async/pending/status prop; it only formats a number it receives
its root is a plain <div> and it declares a prop and fetching behaviour
